scenes.text: This MacBook Pro runs a real coding AI, completely offline.
It's level three of five, from a tiny chip to an AI server, and the first two levels couldn't do this.
That number is memory. An AI model has to fit in memory, and this one has thirty-two gigabytes.
So it runs Qwen3 Coder, a thirty-billion-parameter coding model, in LM Studio. It writes code, explains it, fixes bugs, and nothing leaves the laptop.
For images, it runs FLUX, one of the best open image models, in a free app called Draw Things. Slower than the cloud, but private.
What can't it run? Llama 70B. That needs forty-two gigabytes. It doesn't fit.
Level four has a hundred and twenty-eight. Follow for the next levels.
